what: TIM is one of Brazil's three big mobile operators, selling phone service and home internet across the country, and it acquired part of Oi's mobile business in 2022.
customers: Brazilian households and businesses, mostly on prepaid and postpaid mobile plans.
moat: A three-operator market after the Oi breakup, with spectrum and towers that would cost a fortune to replicate, in a country of 200 million people.
risks: Earnings are exposed to the Brazilian real, which can move sharply against the dollar
Brazilian regulators and courts intervene in telecom pricing and consumer terms
Mobile penetration is already high, so growth has to come from revenue per user
opportunities: 12.6 times earnings and 5.7 times free cash flow with $1.6B of free cash flow
A 16.2% net margin and only $507M of debt against $659M of cash
Analysts see about 24% upside, and prepaid customers keep migrating to higher-value postpaid plans
watch: Postpaid subscriber mix and average revenue per user in local currency.
